title: SecondChance Supplement: Identification Proofs, Causal Audit Contracts and Frozen Evidence
status: v20 explanatory supplement, 2026-10-19. New derivations and routing of frozen v19 evidence; no new experiment or literature search.

sections.heading: S1. Reading route and the recovery contract
paragraphs: The compact manuscript follows an identification question rather than a software-development chronology. Read the endpoint definitions before interpreting a recovery count, the information contract before interpreting a policy, and the denominator before interpreting an area. Sections S2-S7 establish the mathematical contract; S8-S11 connect it to the frozen replay; S12-S13 delimit verification and the next admissible experiment. S14 routes the preserved full manuscript without presenting historical evidence as new confirmation.

The requirement remains fixed when an evaluator is corrected. A requirement change, an unapproved correction or an unavailable archived answer is a different eligibility event. E1 rescoring reuses an old answer; E2 executes a candidate in its own context; E3 executes the integrated current artifact with the surviving lesson and preserved later changes. Agreement of E1 and E2 does not imply E3. Returning a historical verdict to the right value is neither an integration action nor an observation of the current state.

The historical B8 fixture has twelve rescoring improvements and no integrated recoveries from rescoring alone. Selection procedures find twelve development-positive candidates but four initial-state successes. At B5 the strong neutral joint control ties selective recovery with lower work and collateral loss. These retained adverse controls motivate auditing information rather than promoting a repair policy. None is a natural incidence estimate. The historical wording, tables and source-review limits remain unchanged in inherited.paper.

sections.heading: S2. Notation, signed occupation and timing
paragraphs: Fix one of the three utility panels and the same input whenever an identity is reused. A complete identity includes everything on which that panel utility depends. Two identical strings do not prove that the environment is complete or the executor deterministic. Conditional on these assumptions, one state utility is shared across arm visits, templates and checkpoints. This equality constraint can make direct paired bounds tighter than subtracting unrelated area intervals.

The neutral-minus-selective target averages twelve paired normalized utility integrals. Completed-prefix coefficient p integrates [0,t), retaining denominator 12B even when t is small. Current-frequency difference d is an instantaneous arm-occupation difference, not a completed integral. Both vectors sum to zero over a complete identity universe. Remaining fraction r=(B-t)/B is added on the original scale rather than renormalizing the prefix to one.

Commits through integer checkpoint t are revealed before a possible quote; no quote occurs at t=0. Recovery proceeds independently of auditing. A quote at t=B can narrow the final comparison but occupies no positive interval in the left-step width area. Query cap q is a separate upper bound. Dividing area by q, charging a cache quote as an actual worker call, or deleting the unknown suffix after inspecting every currently visible identity would change the experiment.

sections.heading: S3. Exact scenario-conditioned and scenario-union intervals
paragraphs: For a fixed coefficient vector, known contributions are fixed and each unknown utility lies independently in [0,1]. A positive coefficient is minimized at zero and maximized at one; a negative coefficient makes the opposite choices. Coordinatewise extrema give Li and Ui below. Their difference is the unknown absolute-coefficient mass, and each endpoint is attainable in this audit-only box model. Additional semantic or joint-panel restrictions can shrink the box and make these endpoints conservative for that stronger model.

Along c(lambda), the unknown absolute-coefficient mass is convex, so its maximum on the closed segment occurs at lambda zero or one. This proves W_cond, the worst width after the scenario is fixed. It excludes movement of the known contribution between scenarios. Auditing every original state can therefore make W_cond zero while leaving the final coefficient vector unknown.

Now fix revealed utilities and vary both lambda and the unknown utilities. The lower endpoint is linear plus concave min terms in lambda; its minimum occurs at an endpoint. The upper endpoint is linear plus convex max terms; its maximum also occurs at an endpoint. The parameter domain is connected and the contrast is a continuous scalar map. Its attainable union is thus an interval, not merely two disconnected endpoint intervals, with extremes min(L0,L1) and max(U0,U1). W_union is exact under the segment and utility-box assumptions and is at least W_cond.

The order of operations matters: taking a within-scenario range and then its maximum differs from taking a range across all scenarios. Calling both robustness erases which uncertainty remains. The realized premium W_union-W_cond is nonnegative but need not be positive on a particular saved panel.
equations: L_i = sum_(s in A) c_(i,s) u_s + sum_(s in A^c) min(c_(i,s),0)
U_i = sum_(s in A) c_(i,s) u_s + sum_(s in A^c) max(c_(i,s),0)
W_("cond")(A) = max_(i in {0,1}) sum_(s in A^c) abs(c_(i,s))
W_("union")(A;u_A) = max_(i in {0,1}) U_i - min_(i in {0,1}) L_i

sections.heading: S4. Deriving the four-pair pre-outcome objective
paragraphs: The selector is deliberately utility-blind, even to values from previous quotes. Queried identities are retained, while payloads go to a separate interval evaluator. The planning objective therefore maximizes realized union width over every possible u_A. It is conservative under this chosen restriction, not a claim that every adaptive policy must discard legally observed outcomes.

Expand max_i Ui-min_j Lj as a maximum over four ordered pairs (i,j). Finitely many pairs allow maximization over u_A to commute with this maximum. For a pair, the known term is sum over A of (c_i-c_j)u_s. Maximizing each term on [0,1] gives max(c_i-c_j,0). The unknown-coordinate contribution is already a sum of positive upper and negative lower coefficients. Calling these terms K_ij and H_ij yields F below.

The diagonal pairs recover within-scenario unknown absolute masses. An off-diagonal pair can dominate by combining an upper endpoint under one scenario with a lower endpoint under the other. No utility sample, probability prior or learned surrogate is required. If coefficient scenarios were not a line segment, four endpoint pairs would not generally exhaust the class.

A one-query rule compares F after each eligible single addition and waits if no strict improvement exists. A visible-set rule considers currently available subsets within remaining quote cap and public opportunities, minimizes F, prefers fewer quotes and lexicographically earlier identities, and executes only the first planned quote now. It replans at the next visible prefix. This is exact static subset planning, not a schedule over hypothetical future arrivals or a globally optimal causal policy.

sections.heading: S5. Analytic separation, observed zero and feasibility
paragraphs: The preserved analytic construction has c0=(1/4,-1/4), c1=(-1/4,1/4), both original states audited and u=(1,0). Within-scenario unknown mass is zero at both endpoints. The contrast changes continuously from 1/4 to -1/4 as lambda varies, giving union width 1/2. This proves separation without producing an observed path, a thirteenth template or a failure-rate estimate.

The saved replay says something different: all 1,620 actual fixed-panel union premiums are zero. They reuse twelve templates, aggregate prefix geometry and three panels. Their zero premiums do not refute the construction; the construction does not supply positive empirical incidence. F can still differ on a saved prefix because it considers quote outcomes other than the actually observed utilities.

The envelope supplement checks 1,104 visible subsets and 11,159 known-utility vertices. Visibility now is weaker than reachability by the past one-quote-per-checkpoint schedule. The maximum counterfactual premium 1/3 uses a subset flagged not past-reachable; the maximum among past-reachable planning subsets is 1/5. Neither is a premium of an observed actual panel. Keep these flags attached when reusing an illustrative number.

A lawful action selects a visible unaudited identity now. A static visible subset can compare current plans but cannot retroactively create enough earlier opportunities to make it already audited. Planning possibility, historically feasible audit sets and realized outcomes are three distinct objects. Confusing them turns a geometric witness into an unsupported policy gain.

sections.heading: S6. Zero-sum L1 tubes: bound, attainment and invariant ranking
paragraphs: A zero-sum perturbation with L1 norm at most epsilon has equal positive and negative masses, each at most epsilon/2. With utilities in [0,1], its largest contribution is at most epsilon/2 and its smallest at least -epsilon/2. Equivalently, subtracting utility midpoint 1/2 removes the constant by zero-sum and leaves a coordinatewise magnitude bound.

For attainment with fixed audited utilities, the declared class allows two fresh unaudited coordinates, freely valued as one and zero. Put positive mass epsilon/2 on the former and negative mass on the latter for the upper shift; reverse signs for the lower shift. Leave the original coefficients at an original bound-attaining endpoint. Both fixed-scenario and scenario-union widths increase by exactly epsilon. Maximizing over audited outcomes adds the same epsilon to F.

Equality requires these coordinates, utility extremes and perturbation to be simultaneously allowed. The tube is not intersected with an independently established physically realizable continuation class. If fresh identities are forbidden, utilities cannot reach the extremes or actual occupations constrain perturbations, the upper-bound argument may survive while equality fails. If a candidate could audit the only extremal coordinates, the common-addition argument also needs rechecking.

With epsilon=2*eta*r, fixed eta and the same r for every compared candidate set, every objective receives the identical addition. Minimizers and ties remain unchanged. Enlarging a common radius can include more outcomes without changing the action. Choosing candidate-specific radii after outcomes would define a different, outcome-dependent policy and is not an evaluated repair here.

For the preserved two-state example, epsilon=1/5 changes conditioned width from zero to 1/5 and union width from 1/2 to 7/10. Positive and negative masses are each 1/10. These are arithmetic consequences of a mathematical construction, not new state-audit data.

sections.heading: S7. The unrestricted safe interval and what it does not identify
paragraphs: Restricted selection cannot certify its own continuation assumption. The evaluator retains an unrestricted future suffix. K_t is the quoted signed prefix contribution. Add negative unknown prefix coefficients for the lower endpoint and positive ones for the upper endpoint. Each arm has a remaining normalized utility contribution in [0,r]; their difference is in [-r,r]. Adding it yields the safe interval below.

Safe width is the unknown prefix L1 mass plus 2r. A single available quote removes its absolute prefix coefficient. Unrestricted one-step minimax is therefore prefix_abs. Inspecting all visible identities cannot eliminate the suffix: future states may still be unseen. With arbitrarily prompt transitions to disjoint fresh identities, the worst suffix is a supremum or closure argument. A positive minimum transition delay or physical transition constraint can change attainment.

A B4/t1 construction has both arms sharing an audited utility-1/2 state through the common prefix. Compatible worlds exchange utility-one and utility-zero occupations after cost two, giving final contrasts +1/2 and -1/2. A rule reading only that common prefix cannot certify the sign in both worlds. This does not imply every online instance is unidentified or that this outer interval is sharp under a more restricted transition graph.

At the terminal checkpoint, r=0 and the fixed-path direct audit-only interval is sharp under common deterministic utility and the box model. Earlier intervals are online outer bounds. If logs, equality or utility assumptions fail, a narrow interval or positive sign cannot continue to be called certified.

sections.heading: S8. Nine causal policies and a complementarity warning
paragraphs: All nine rules share identities, arrivals and quote caps. Frozen deterministic rules break score ties by ascending identity. Previously queried identities are retained, but neither their payloads nor hidden program semantics enter selection. A bound evaluator receives lawful quote values after the action is fixed. Replacing hidden future records or utility payloads while preserving the public prefix must leave actions unchanged.

One-step and set rules optimize different action spaces. A planned set contains only identities already visible and fits remaining quotes and public opportunities. Only its first member is queried; the plan can change with new arrivals. This is not an offline schedule computed from the final path. Conversely, the arrival-constrained oracle knows final coefficients and remains a lower bound, not a tenth causal competitor.

The restricted objective exhibits complementarity in a four-state construction with endpoints (1/4,-1/4,0,0) and (0,0,1/4,-1/4). Initial worst width is 1/2. Quoting the first positive-coordinate state leaves the other endpoint at 1/2; quoting the other alone also gives zero gain. Quoting both reduces the worst width to 1/4. The second quote thus gains 1/4 after the first and zero beforehand. A zero-gain stopping rule can miss a useful pair.

The construction respects zero-sum coefficients and can use remaining fraction 1/2 and active-frequency difference (-1/2,1/2,1/2,-1/2). It is a property test, not an observed common failure. It explains why an adaptive-submodularity guarantee [21] cannot be transferred without proving its required conditions for this objective and information model.

sections.heading: S9. Checkpoint width area and the B8/q3 case
paragraphs: For width area J, a width observed after any quote at integer t applies to the left-step interval [t,t+1). Sum checkpoints zero through B-1 and divide by B. W_B is a separate terminal endpoint. J is neither continuous elapsed audit time nor expected recovery utility: it accounts for identification width on a stipulated recovery-cost grid.

The union-one B8/q3 widths contributing to J are 2, 7/4, 3/2, 5/4, 1, 5/6, 7/12 and 1/3. Their sum is 37/4, so J=37/32. Checkpoint six has safe width 7/12; the terminal checkpoint eight has width 1/12. Substituting one for the other is a timing error. W_8 is excluded from J because no following positive interval remains inside the horizon.

Restricted one differs only at checkpoint five: 7/8 instead of 5/6, a difference of 1/24. The union improvement is therefore 1/(24*8)=1/192. Both use checkpoints four, five and six, three quotes and final width 1/12. This is an information-allocation change in the saved replay, not a measured audit-cost saving.

Late-prefix quotes at six, seven and eight, reaches final width 1/24 and the positive unaffected certificate at eight, but has J=75/64. Relative to 37/32, area is worse by 1/64. The last quote cannot repair uncertainty accumulated earlier. Reporting only final width conceals this intermediate-information cost.

Recovery intervention work, distinct-state cache quotes, subset computations, verifier work and elapsed latency are separate columns. The horizon is not decremented by a cache quote. A deployed protocol must declare whether audits pause recovery, overlap it or consume shared resources before interpreting J as an operational objective.

Delta means union minus restricted; negative area is narrower intermediate uncertainty. All final-width and quote-count differences are zero. Every pair uses the same quote checkpoints. The four decreases are B8/q2 one and set, B8/q3 one and B8/q4 one, each exactly 1/192. Twelve areas tie, including every B5 pairing. No additional unaffected positive certificate appears. These results support a limited allocation effect, not a winning final-width policy.

The sixteen rows are dependent contracts over exposed paths, not sixteen independent replications or Bernoulli trials. They cannot supply a population confidence interval or a native-method leaderboard. The broader seventy-two-configuration family includes all nine policies. Its Pareto statements apply only to that family and its width/area/quote axes. The two-quote current-disagreement rule at B8/q3 remains nondominated because resources are one of those axes.

sections.heading: S11. Eta sensitivity: denominator, retrospective fit and leakage
paragraphs: The saved aggregate views are checkpoints zero through five at B5 and zero through eight at B8: fifteen total. At the two terminal views r=0, the prefix equals the final coefficient and membership is trivial. Excluding them gives thirteen nonterminal views. That denominator includes two checkpoint-zero views, although no quote is permitted then. The eleven nonterminal query-time views are a different denominator.

At eta zero, membership tests the exact segment: every nonzero-slope coordinate must imply the same lambda in [0,1], and zero-slope coordinates must already equal the final coefficient. Equivalently, minimize L1 distance from the final vector to the segment. Its exact piecewise-linear endpoint and weighted-median breakpoints suffice for comparison with 2*eta*r. Evaluation uses the union of prefix, current and final identities; final identities remain unavailable to the selector.

Every eta row reuses the same thirteen dependent views. Inclusion grows from four to thirteen because the declared set expands. It is neither a coverage probability nor validation of a stochastic transition model. Choosing eta=1/2 because this table reaches 13/13 would inspect the outcomes needed for an independent calibration check. Repeating snapshots or adding the trivial terminal memberships cannot fix that leakage.

The grid was fixed for this diagnostic. A prospective calibration claim needs eta chosen on disjoint histories or an independently justified continuation class, frozen before future coefficients arrive and checked on reserved correction families with all violations retained. Until then, restricted objectives remain diagnostic and only unrestricted intervals certify replay comparisons.

sections.heading: S12. Verification ledger and assumption-failure checks
paragraphs: The scientific inputs remain 168 authored traces and five frozen support records, bound by 173 input hashes. The v19 result SHA256 is 82115c85bd66c798c897ce8827f7a270f2a3a46dbaf05ceb03aa966ba976d9d8. This v20 edit does not rerun the experiment, mutate a sealed output or generate another audit. Input, analysis and verifier snapshots remain in the v19 run.

The primary same-author separate implementation checks 540 decisions, 1,620 safe-bound cells and 1,620 union cells, plus 2,243 known-utility vertices, 5,259 lambda-breakpoint checks and 22,968 unknown-utility completions. It checks ninety memberships, seventy-two finite-family Pareto rows and fifty-six old terminal reproductions. These are computational checks, not independent experimental units.

The envelope verifier addresses sets not visited by selected policies: 1,104 visible subsets, 11,159 known-utility vertices, 6,624 tube-attainment checks and ninety common-eta ranking checks. Past-feasibility flags remain explicit. Its larger premium on an unreachable set is not presented as an implementable gain. Separate code and input locks keep this supplementary calculation distinct from primary verification.

A checksum supplies local byte agreement, not complete environment capture or external scientific review. Hidden commits invalidate the occupation partition; omitted state or stochastic behavior can invalidate common utility. Missing positive-duration observations require endpoints rather than a filled-in point estimate. Any truth outside an unrestricted interval must stop certification and trigger investigation, not be relabeled a model outlier.

Failed historical attempts remain in the preserved record. They are useful for reproduction but cannot be pooled as independent confirmation. New actual audits, worker/model calls, fits, natural histories, independent units and physical latency measurements remain zero. No real private professor consultation occurred; named methodological lenses and critic judgments are not evidence.

sections.heading: S13. Prospective study and explicit falsification criteria
paragraphs: This is a proposed protocol, not a completed study. Require a fixed requirement, authenticated old rejection, separately approved evaluator correction, available candidate archive and complete current-state snapshot. Preserve no-useful-reject, no-written-lesson, disputed-correction, missing-archive and failed-integration cases in the inclusion flow. Repository issues or stronger tests alone do not provide correction-history labels [17,18].

Freeze families, resource envelopes, action rules, ties and eta calibration before protected outcomes. Selectors receive matched public streams; the evaluator receives only lawfully disclosed values. Separate candidate execution, integration, lesson edits, retries, worker calls, elapsed time and failures. For stochastic states, define repeated within-state sampling and the expected-utility target before uncertainty intervals. A deterministic fixture score cannot supply that contract.

Jointly report integrated-state utility, preserved-capability loss, total work, final audit width, certificate time and any prespecified operational area. Do not switch endpoints when late-prefix wins only final width or a neutral rule wins cost. Reserve independent correction families, not repeated checkpoints, for confirmation. Set sample-size and smallest-effect rules only after obtaining an admissible sampling unit; the current 168 files are not natural histories.

Reject superiority if neutral controls retain their advantage, lineage fails to localize useful rejects, or added work outweighs the declared benefit. Reject identification if held outcomes fall outside safe intervals, state equality fails or actions read hidden futures. Reject exact tube attainment if allowed transitions cannot realize the fresh-coordinate construction. Preserve failures and nonattainment. A favorable critic cannot reverse those gates.

sections.heading: S14. Main-to-supplement routing and the preserved full record
paragraphs: The compact main carries the assumptions and negative results needed to assess its claim without a development chronology. S3-S4 explains the three widths; S5-S7 separates mathematical possibility, actual outcomes and safe certificates; S8-S11 makes policies and denominators inspectable. The Korean guide adds hand calculations before preserving its earlier text.

The renderer appends inherited.paper after these new sections. It is an exact object copy of the complete v19 paper, including title, subtitle, abstract, all sections, appendices, tables, figures and twenty-one reference objects. That block is labeled historical full evidence. Its chronology is not a second current main paper or an independent cohort. A v17/v19 heading there describes the source; the compact main is v20.

All reference numbers, texts, URLs and reviewed claim scopes are unchanged. Abstract-only literature-review limits remain explicit. These new sections derive our saved-evidence contract; they do not silently expand external full-text review or transfer reported external effects. paper.abstract: Correcting an evaluator does not establish recovery of the current agent state. SecondChance separates historical rescoring, integrated-state audits and the information available to an audit selector. Earlier authored experiments and partial-observation diagnostics retain twelve histories, 168 policy paths and nine complete state identities. V16 introduced three selectors without future commits. V17 asks what a robust selector actually protects when the continuation model can be wrong. We prove that one-query minimax under unrestricted future states reduces to the existing absolute-prefix rule, then implement a restricted persistence/cancellation segment with one-query and visible-set minimax allocation. Alongside FIFO, current-state disagreement, persistence ranking and a last-opportunity prefix control, seven policies yield 56 dependent configurations, 420 decisions and 1, 260 unrestricted safe bounds. The restricted segment excludes the actual final coefficient vector in nine of thirteen nonterminal views. At horizon eight and quote cap three, late-prefix reaches width 1/24 and a positive certificate at checkpoint eight; restricted minimax reaches 1/12 and no certificate. Waiting increases normalized checkpoint uncertainty area from 37/32 for restricted-set to75/64. A four-state construction shows zero individual minimax gains but a positive two-query gain, so a diminishing-returns assumption cannot be silently transferred. All safe bounds use the unrestricted future suffix, irrespective of selection model. Exact verification preserves the prior negative evidence and distinguishes conditional robustness, final width, certificate delay and cached quote cost. Actual prospective audits and natural histories added remain zero; no population recovery or scheduling superiority is claimed. The continuation separates unknown-scenario objectives and shows no final-width gain in16 paired contracts; uniform L1 inflation changes model inclusion but not candidate rankings.
contributions: A state-bound recovery contract separating saved-answer rescoring, fresh candidate execution and fresh integrated-state audits, with strong neutral controls and all-template denominators.
An executed controlled-censoring study on nine complete state identities across 168 exposed authored paths: 512 audit sets per budget/panel and 3,072 exactly checked contrast bounds.

Sharp audit-only contrast endpoints that preserve shared-state dependence, plus retrospective minimum audit certificates and explicit counterexamples when complete-log or deterministic-state assumptions are removed.

A reproducible continuation of the v11/v12 negative results: fresh committed-state observations, two signs of sampling error, neutral ties/advantages, preserved failed attempts and a staged natural-model confirmation protocol.

A predeclared utility-blind coefficient schedule achieves the minimum fixed-cardinality contrast width and separates exact-width optimality from outcome-dependent sign stopping and retrospective certificates.

A prefix-only audit interface, unknown-future suffix bound and causal replay with exact arrival-feasible oracle comparison; counterexamples prevent transferring offline greedy optimality to an online setting.

A conditional robust-allocation benchmark that separates worst scenario-conditioned width from unknown-scenario identification, tests continuation misspecification, exposes query complementarity and compares delayed cheap audits with their uncertainty-time cost.

The continuation distinguishes the worst width conditional on a fixed scenario, the union of identification intervals when the scenario itself is unknown, and a pre-outcome worst union objective used for utility-blind audit selection. The last has four endpoint-pair cases; a two-state analytic construction separates zero conditioned width from union width1/2. This mathematical construction must not be substituted for observed incidence.

sections.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: An evaluator patch can reverse yesterday's rejection while leaving today's system broken. Consider a correct signed-arithmetic implementation that was rejected because an evaluator compared its answer against an absolute value. The incumbent remains the wrong program; a later, valid output-format fix may already have been applied; and a lesson written from the rejection may still recommend the wrong procedure. Rescoring the archived answer changes the historical verdict. It does not execute an integration, preserve the later fix or withdraw the lesson. A deployment decision therefore requires a behavioral endpoint on the actual current state, rather than a corrected score alone.

This distinction matters for systems that update persistent textual state. SkillOpt gates bounded skill edits on validation and retains rejected edits as feedback [1]; Reflexion conditions future trials on feedback-derived reflective memory [2]. Self-Refine and CRITIC improve outputs through different feedback loops [3,4], while SCoRe learns correction behavior through online reinforcement learning [6]. These mechanisms motivate inspecting decisions and memory after an evaluator correction. They do not by themselves answer the narrower identification question studied here: after the requirement remains fixed and its evaluator is corrected, what evidence establishes that an archived alternative has actually repaired the integrated current state?

We make that question executable before testing it on language models. SecondChance is a small deterministic research instrument with an immutable requirement, authored faulty/corrected evaluators, a fixed archive, logged state commits and fresh state audits. It separates E1, rescoring the same saved output; E2, freshly invoking a candidate; and E3, auditing the integrated artifact with its surviving lesson and valid later changes. Figure 1 depicts these endpoints. The construction permits exact inspection and falsification of a measurement contract, but supplies no estimate of natural evaluator faults, LLM recovery probability or method superiority.

We ask three linked questions. RQ1: can saved-score and fresh-candidate success disagree with integrated-state recovery? RQ2: does lineage-first joint repair beat a strong neutral early-stop procedure under the same authored caps? RQ3: when recovery is summarized over intervention cost, how much can a coarse observation grid hide? Twelve authored histories yield 168 nested policy-budget paths. The neutral procedure ties terminal recovery and is better on cost and collateral loss at budget five. A follow-up freezes every path and makes 292 new state audits. It reveals both missed recovery and understated collateral degradation, with discrepancies covered by a conditional commit-geometry bound. Thus the paper's contribution is a falsifiable recovery measurement and control protocol, including negative policy evidence, rather than a demonstrated new LLM recovery algorithm.

Incomplete observation raises a further decision: which policy comparisons remain warranted when some state audits are unavailable? Version 14 addresses this question by deliberately deleting saved observations from the exposed deterministic paths. It treats unknown utilities as unknown, retains equality for the same complete state and fixed input, and bounds the policy contrast directly. An individual area can remain uncertain even when common uncertainty cancels from a paired comparison. This is a new finite diagnostic, not a new agent recovery experiment.

The v14 minimum audit subsets were selected retrospectively using the complete outcomes. That does not supply a deployable order. V15 instead constructs an order using complete logged state identities and occupation coefficients before revealing panel utilities. The distinction is narrow but consequential: a width-optimal known-path schedule can be implemented without utility leakage, yet it still need not match the cheapest outcome-specific sign certificate or operate before future commits are known.

V17 makes the robustness assumption itself inspectable. An unrestricted one-step minimax criterion reduces to prefix_abs; a restricted persistence/cancellation model changes decisions but misses many actual continuations. A cheap rule that waits for the last public query opportunities can narrow the terminal interval while carrying greater intermediate uncertainty. Figure 8 separates these outcomes from real prospective audit savings.

At budget eight, selection arms have 12/12 development-positive candidates but 4/12 initial-state recoveries, while rescoring alone restores 0/12. sections.heading: Related Work
paragraphs: We organize comparisons by the decision each method changes, the feedback it may access and the object it evaluates. This avoids treating every reflection or verification method as an interchangeable repair baseline. Our twenty references support particular design choices; their reported benchmark numbers are not pooled with our executor results.

sections.heading: Correction, selection and persistent memory
paragraphs: Self-Refine uses one model to generate, critique and refine an output [3]; CRITIC incorporates tool interaction when validating and revising an output [4]. Huang et al. examine intrinsic reasoning self-correction without external feedback [5]. Their scope is narrower than all correction, especially in light of later learned correction strategies such as SCoRe [6]. Our evaluator correction is an explicit external event, and our current study runs no language model. These papers motivate controlling feedback and update rights; neither their successes nor their limitations can be imported as our empirical result.

Verifier-based selection ranks generated candidate solutions [7]. SkillOpt instead optimizes a persistent skill document through bounded edits and a validation gate, with rejected-edit feedback retained for later updates [1]. Consequently, retaining rejected candidates is not our novelty claim. We audit what a changed evaluator requires after those decisions: immutable old outputs, a common current-state fork, actual integration, preserved later changes and a fresh integrated-state outcome. The fixture is a fixed-pool experiment; generating a new corrective skill remains a separate comparison.

Reflexion provides the closest motivation for examining feedback-derived lessons [2]. Zep maintains temporally scoped facts and invalidates inconsistent edges when information changes [8]. Our setting holds the requirement fixed and corrects its erroneous implementation; world-state change and evaluator correction have different approval conditions. We therefore test a same-artifact retain/suspend lesson fork and leave native Reflexion, Zep and SkillOpt reproduction unmeasured.

sections.heading: Evaluation validity and executable correctness
paragraphs: Proxy optimization can improve a development score without improving a separately evaluated objective [9]. Model-selection bias and adaptive holdout reuse make evaluation access part of the method, rather than an implementation detail [10,11]. These motivate freezing candidate pools, audit inputs and disclosure boundaries. Our researcher can inspect every fixture label; controller non-use is documented but is not independent adjudication or a secret final test.

EvalPlus shows why finite code tests can miss incorrect implementations [17]. SWE-bench supplies repository issue-resolution tasks that could support a richer future environment [18], but neither resource automatically labels an old evaluator as wrong under an unchanged requirement. Such labels, the historical rejected edits and their downstream lessons must be collected separately. ReAct's interleaving of reasoning and environment actions also makes clear why a prompt or program hash alone may omit relevant agent state [19].

sections.heading: Resource curves and reproducible comparisons
paragraphs: Henderson et al. emphasize nondeterminism and reporting variability [12]; Agarwal et al. address uncertainty in aggregate few-run comparisons [13]. We retain history-level denominators and avoid confidence intervals that would falsely turn designed templates into sampled natural histories. Local process counts and wall durations are execution resources, not additional independent trials.

Performance profiles compare distributions of a declared performance metric [14], and COCO makes problem instances, targets and function-call runtime explicit [15,16]. Those ideas motivate reporting both terminal behavior and an intervention-cost curve. Our integrated utility can decrease after a repair, unlike a retained best-so-far objective; hitting a target once does not guarantee its subsequent persistence. The area and geometry bound below are our conditional measurement argument, not a theorem imported from numerical-optimization benchmarks.

Partial identification concerns the values compatible with observed information and assumptions; sampling uncertainty is a separate issue. The distinction between an identification region and confidence coverage is explicit in the primary abstract of Imbens and Manski [20]. Our fixed authored cohort supplies no sampling-based population confidence interval, and we do not implement their inferential procedures.

sections.heading: Problem Formulation
paragraphs: The unit of comparison is a frozen history under a verified correction to a fixed requirement. The state includes the executable artifact and any active lesson that affects routing. Correction eligibility, selection success and current recovery are separate predicates.

sections.heading: Correction eligibility and behavioral endpoints
paragraphs: The unchanged requirement G is exact signed addition of a/b and c/d. The response grammar permits a bounded signed integer, decimal or nonzero-denominator fraction after FINAL=. Numerically equivalent rational forms are accepted, so FINAL=-2/3 and FINAL=-4/6 denote the same value. Parsing uses a bounded grammar and Python Fraction; response text is never evaluated as code. Non-numeric values, zero denominators, excessive numeric lengths and arbitrary prefixes are rejected. Approximate decimal values are not silently accepted as exact rationals.

The authored defect replaces the exact signed target with its absolute value. Under the negative development sum, an absolute-value program is accepted while an exact signed program is rejected. The accepted correction removes that absolute-value operation while preserving the task and valid-answer contract. Old outputs and old decisions are appended to, never replaced by corrected scores. A change in requested sign, task identity, accepted alternatives or evaluation objective would instead define a new task or a disputed correction and must not be counted as the same correction event.

Correction eligibility in this fixture follows from the authored arithmetic contract, not independent human review. In an empirical scientific-label setting, the fixed requirement, counterexample, old assertion, corrected assertion and valid alternatives would need a separate adjudication procedure. A model critic agreeing with the correction would not provide that independence. Ambiguous annotations, requirements changes and unsupported corrections should remain pending rather than become useful-rejection evidence.

Endpoint E1 is V_new applied to the exact same saved response bytes; it measures historical score change. Endpoint E2 is an actual fresh candidate invocation on permitted development data; it measures what that candidate newly does under its own state. Endpoint E3 is a fresh audit of the integrated current-state checkpoint, including retained lessons and routing. E2 can be positive for a development-memorizing candidate while E3 fails on a different input. E1 has no state-transition semantics at all.

sections.heading: Complete state and decision lineage
paragraphs: A checkpoint contains a program operation, the lesson text and its active/absent/suspended status, and a valid later change that must survive repair. The latter fixes the FINAL= output prefix and the JSON trace format. Candidate artifacts encode exact rational addition, absolute-value addition, development-input memorization, integer truncation or a constant zero response. Each candidate runs in a separate local Python process. Its request bytes, response bytes, state hash, worker hash, return code and observed process duration are recorded.

The history records the candidate archive, saved outputs, old accept/reject events, incumbent and any actually written fixture lesson. The fixed authored lesson writer can record the instruction to fall back to the absolute-value solver for opposite-sign addition. This is not a model reflection. The initial audit uses negative same-sign terms; the later panel uses opposite-sign terms with a negative total. The constructed lesson can therefore preserve initial success after integration yet break success on the later input. All those task values and the writer rule are visible to the researcher.

Lineage is also explicitly authored. An aligned hint points to the useful exact candidate; a misleading hint points to the development-memorizing candidate. Every policy receives the same hint and archive. The neutral policy chooses not to use the hint for its ordering. This design exposes the consequences of reliable versus unreliable localization; it does not learn a localization model or estimate the prevalence of good historical lineage.

A saved rescore and a candidate invocation do not themselves mutate the incumbent. Only the logged integration and lesson-suspension events can change this fixture state. Integration verifies the candidate artifact and preserved valid-change hash. A common parent hash binds all policy forks. The pre-lesson checkpoint and final checkpoint are retained separately. This complete state definition is a testable assumption, not a property guaranteed for general agents with filesystem state, latent memory, tools or external services.

sections.heading: Method: A Recovery Audit Contract
paragraphs: The instrument runs matched intervention procedures and observes state-bound outcomes. It does not use a critic's agreement as evidence of correctness. A policy result is identified only relative to a recorded state, allowed information, intervention budget, audit panel and failure/missingness rule.

sections.heading: Endpoint denominators and the lesson contrast
paragraphs: A current initial recovery requires success on the fresh initial-input audit of the integrated state. The main all-started burden counts no initial recovery or failure on the later-input panel. It keeps templates without useful rejected candidates in the denominator. Conditional persistence failure divides the number of initial successes that fail later by the number of initial successes; zero initial successes yield null, not zero. Joint initial-success/later-failure frequency and total later failure are separate all-template quantities.

The label later refers to a different input executed against the same final checkpoint. No further agent evolution, model training, new selection or calendar-time drift occurs between the initial and later panels. Thus the stored strict_recurrence field denotes cross-panel maintenance failure in the fixture. It is not a measured long-term evolutionary recurrence rate. A future recurrence study must specify the subsequent evolution process and preserve its additional decisions, exposure and resources.

Unaffected-task performance is paired before and after intervention. Absolute failure after repair and incremental loss from the same baseline are different quantities. This matters because selecting a development-memorizing program can destroy an unaffected positive-addition capability even when the corrected development score is perfect. Templates with such collateral losses remain in every relevant table.

The fixed-artifact lesson contrast is built only after selection and integration have happened once. The exact pre-lesson bytes are copied into retain and suspend branches, preserving program artifact, valid later changes, routing and allowance. Selection is not rerun. This controls the integration mediator that would otherwise differ between whole procedures. In a general model experiment, treatment assignment, context length, allowed correction knowledge and memory retrieval would also need explicit control. Here the mechanism is visibly authored in the worker, so its contrast verifies implementation rather than discovering an LLM memory mechanism.

sections.heading: Cost-indexed recovery utility
paragraphs: Version 11 observes the current state at policy-cost coordinates 0, B/4, B/2, 3B/4 and B and computes a normalized left-step area. A terminal success can therefore have zero recorded area. For example, an initially failing state integrated successfully at cost four under cap five is still failing at the last left endpoint 3.75 and successful only at the final observation five. The resulting zero is correct for the declared coarse statistic, but it is not the area of the complete committed-state path.

Let c_i be every committed-state cost, including zero and a terminal boundary B. Let s_i be the state in force after c_i, held until the next commit. If the log contains every state mutation, the worker is a pure deterministic function of that state and the fixed audit input, and each positive-duration state has actually been freshly audited, then the state-path area is identified by the observed step sum. This is a conditional statement about this executor and panel. It is not a claim that one output identifies a stochastic agent's expected capability.

The argument is direct: partition the cost axis at every complete state commit. The executor and input do not change within each resulting interval, so its binary output is constant there. A fresh observed value for that state supplies the interval's utility, and integration over the finite partition gives A_C. Audits are not inferred from saved-score positives or candidate identifiers. A missing positive-duration audit leaves its area contribution unknown in [0,width/B]. A missing state that exists only at the endpoint B can leave the area defined while the terminal score remains missing.

The cost axis excludes the common external audit envelope. Adding audit spending retroactively to the controller's five- or eight-unit axis would change the estimand and possibly the feasible repair procedure. We instead report actual audit subprocess counts and elapsed time as a separate resource vector. These are local process measurements, not model tokens, billed dollars or a paired hardware-speed benchmark.

sections.heading: Commit reconstruction and an error bound
paragraphs: For each coarse cell [g_j,g_(j+1)), let t_j be its first strictly interior state-changing commit. If there is no such commit, set t_j to the right boundary. A commit at a coarse grid point is already observed there, and a metadata event leaving the state bytes unchanged creates no new exposure interval. Until t_j the state equals the coarse left-endpoint state. Afterwards each bounded utility can differ from that left value by at most one. Summing those potentially exposed lengths proves the bound below without a monotonicity assumption.

The bound is sharp in a one-change cell: a utility jump from zero to one, or from one to zero, at the first interior commit persists through the cell. For the budget-five integration at four, the exposed interval is [4,5), yielding E=1/5. A coarse initial-area value of zero and a freshly observed commit-aware value of 1/5 attain the bound. Grid-aligned integration at four under budget eight has no initial-area discrepancy because four is already an observed grid point.

Monotone nondecreasing utility implies that a left-step coarse area cannot exceed the complete state-path area. General repair does not guarantee monotonicity. Collateral degradation supplies the reverse-sign counterexample: a state with unaffected utility one can switch to zero between observations, making the coarse area too large. Nor does observing a successful final state rule out an unobserved transient failure or recovery. Full commit logs and fresh values are necessary for the stronger reconstruction claim.

Unknown state-changing events, an incomplete routing/environment snapshot, a fresh same-state response that differs from the earlier response, a missing positive-duration state audit, or a discrepancy exceeding the geometric bound falsifies the corresponding identification step. Such cases should suspend the point estimate; a critic's agreement cannot repair missing observations. Our self-checks include missing positive-width audits, missing terminal-only observations, a decreasing-utility counterexample and unchanged-state commits.

sections.heading: Sharp audit-only bounds with shared state
paragraphs: Fix one audit panel, budget B and the twelve equally weighted authored templates. For each policy p and complete state identity s, let w(p,s) be the normalized time spent in that state, averaged over templates. The panel utility u(s) is binary and shared across visits only under the complete-state, pure deterministic worker and fixed-input assumptions. A known state hash alone does not establish those assumptions. In this new analysis the source observations are checked for concordance, then deliberately hidden according to a declared view.

The information model knows commit times, state identities, policy occupation weights and revealed audit utilities. It does not use the arithmetic source program to infer a hidden score. This restricted audit-only model is essential: the researcher can read the complete fixture and the full saved outcomes, so the experiment measures robustness to controlled disclosure, not irreducible ignorance about an inaccessible deployed system.

Write the neutral-minus-selective mean-area contrast as a signed sum with coefficient c(s)=w(neutral,s)-w(selective,s). Revealed scores contribute K. Each unrevealed utility can be zero or one, subject to equality across the same state. A positive coefficient is minimized at zero and maximized at one; a negative coefficient has the opposite assignment. The resulting endpoints are jointly attainable within this audit-only model. With binary scores the set of compatible contrasts can be discrete: we claim a sharp interval hull, not that every interior real value is attainable.

Bounding each policy independently and subtracting its intervals forgets that the same unknown utility appears in both policies. The direct interval is always contained in that subtraction interval. Exact cancellation does not require that either policy area be identified. This is elementary finite linear optimization over a cube; no priority claim, causal effect identification or external theorem transfer is made.

K = sum_(s in O) c_s u_s
ell = K + sum_(s in M) min(c_s,0)
r = K + sum_(s in M) max(c_s,0)

sections.heading: Experimental Setup
paragraphs: We distinguish the original policy experiment from a later measurement experiment on its frozen paths. Every number below comes from the two retained local execution result files, not an external paper or a new model call. The editorial v13 cycle changes the exposition, figure specification and reviewed references; it does not create new policy trials.

sections.heading: Authored cohort, policies and budgets
paragraphs: The cohort comprises twelve authored templates: eight contain a previously rejected exact candidate and four contain no useful rejected candidate. Candidate position, hint alignment and presence of the written fixture lesson vary. Each archive has four candidates. The same six unique arithmetic inputs serve development, two additional-input checks, the initial audit, later-input audit and unaffected-input audit. Reuse of those inputs across policies does not create independent tasks or histories.

The old receipt labels one call kind independent_authored_qualification. That historical identifier is retained for byte compatibility, but its meaning is restricted here to two additional authored numeric inputs that the controller does not read. The same author, source code and arithmetic rule determine every input and answer. Those checks are neither independently authored correction qualification nor a secret held-out evaluation. Programmatic non-use by the controller is weaker than an access-controlled external audit boundary.

All seven policies receive work-unit caps of five and eight. Rescoring costs one authored unit, a fresh candidate execution two, integration one and lesson treatment one. Selection reserves enough allowance for its fresh execution/integration and, where assigned, lesson action. It stops at the first development-positive candidate, freshly executes that candidate and integrates on development success. Neutral and lineage-first policies share this acceptance rule. Equal caps do not force equal spending. No candidate is newly generated during these fixed-pool procedures.

The selection-by-lesson factorial uses no repair, selection only, lesson only and selective joint repair with V_new in every cell. This is a whole-procedure contrast: data-query ordering, failed selection, reservations and integration can differ across cells. Neutral early-stop and neutral joint are essential additional controls; exhaustive replay alone would be a weak comparator. The rescore-only arm is an endpoint control rather than a candidate recovery procedure.

sections.heading: Frozen-trajectory committed-state re-audit
paragraphs: Before the follow-up, the runner verifies every artifact hash in the prior v11 execution receipt and pins the old worker implementation. It fixes all 168 trajectory files, twelve history records, the three audit inputs and its own analysis code. Every event is replayed from the recorded initial state. Integration checks the archive artifact and preserved valid change; lesson treatment checks its supporting text hash. Reconstructed pre-lesson and final snapshots must exactly equal the authenticated original snapshots. An unrecognized event is rejected because it could hide a state mutation.

For each trajectory separately, every distinct committed-state hash is submitted to a new local worker subprocess on the initial, later and unaffected inputs. There is no audit cache across trajectories. A repeated byte-identical state within a trajectory reuses its new observed result only under the declared deterministic-worker assumption; this reduces redundant subprocesses without pretending that reused observations are independent samples. Every request, stdout, stderr, worker hash, process return code and elapsed duration is preserved.

The new observations are compared with the original coarse observations wherever they bind the same state hash. Drift suspends commit-aware point estimation. The primary analysis compares A_C with the retained A_G on the same frozen policy path, checks the geometric bound for all three panels and reports every initiated template. No policy sees the fresh audit outputs, no candidate is regenerated, no lesson treatment is changed and no failed policy is removed.

The first follow-up attempt stopped after one state subprocess because the adapter initially omitted the reused area function's explicit budget argument. That failed directory, its frozen plan, exact failed analysis-code bytes and failure record are preserved. The corrected complete attempt uses a new directory. Its 292 state subprocesses are reported separately from that one completed subprocess in an incomplete attempt. No incomplete attempt is counted as a successful trajectory or discarded from the execution history.

sections.heading: Analysis unit and resource accounting
paragraphs: The first experiment contains twelve authored history templates, seven procedures and two caps: 12 × 7 × 2 = 168 trajectories. They reuse six unique authored arithmetic inputs. The state follow-up reuses three of those panel inputs, auditing 292 distinct states within trajectories and producing 876 outputs. Neither repeated policies, panel outputs nor subprocess invocations enlarge the independent history sample. The template construction varies availability of a useful rejection, lesson presence, archive order and aligned/misleading lineage; it does not sample those factors from deployment.

The action schedule charges one unit per rescore, two per candidate invocation, one per integration and one per lesson treatment. These are authored work units. We report realized spending under equal caps, because forcing equal spending would remove early stopping as an outcome. Common external audits have a separate ledger: the first experiment used 840 coarse-checkpoint calls plus 24 same-artifact memory audits; its total 1,048 subprocesses also includes candidate/qualification work. The successful follow-up uses 292 state subprocesses. No provider costs or hardware-calibrated efficiency ratios are inferred.

All selected tables are generated from frozen summaries, with all twelve started histories in each row. A zero conditional-recovery denominator is null. No-repair, rescore-only and lesson-only arms remain even when their recovery area is zero. The incomplete first follow-up attempt remains outside successful aggregates and is explicitly reported in the reproducibility appendix.

sections.heading: Controlled omission protocol
paragraphs: Before calculating omission outcomes, a new plan and exact analysis/test code are frozen with byte snapshots of all 168 v12 traces, their receipts/results, the original worker and the v13 paper/source/claim records. The new run uses only the Python standard library and invokes neither a worker nor a model endpoint. All prior receipt-listed outputs are authenticated. Current source files are rechecked after the analysis. The successful exact computation takes about 12.89 seconds on one local host; this is not an algorithmic efficiency comparison.

There are nine unique complete state hashes across the entire fixed cohort. A revealed global state audit discloses its three fixed-panel scores and can inform every identical-state visit under the declared deterministic contract. We enumerate all 512 observed-state subsets for each budget and panel. This produces 3072 bound rows, not 3072 independent tests. The earlier v12 execution deliberately made no cross-trajectory audit cache; reusing its now-available deterministic observations is a new analysis rule, not a retrospective reduction of that execution cost.

Six predeclared views reveal all states, no states, initial states, terminal states, prior coarse-grid states, or states whose first hexadecimal hash digit is even. These rules inspect identity, position or time, not score values. They are controlled sensitivity interventions; no missing-at-random mechanism or probability of real omission is fitted. For each subset the formula is compared with exhaustive compatible binary completions, the full-data value must be contained, and revealing another audit must not widen the interval.

Retrospective certificate searches report the smallest revealed-state count that exactly identifies a contrast, establishes neutral noninferiority, establishes strict neutral advantage, or identifies both individual areas. A certificate uses the known source outcomes to evaluate candidate observation sets. It is not an adaptive sampling algorithm, a prospective stopping rule or a demonstrated way to reduce real audit expenditure. Source outcomes never guide a new policy, and no frozen recovery decision is changed.

sections.heading: Results and Analysis
paragraphs: We report the endpoint separation and policy negative result before the new area analysis. This ordering prevents a more informative measurement from being mistaken for an improved controller.

sections.heading: Saved-score improvement is not current-state recovery
paragraphs: The completed v11 run contains 1,048 local subprocess calls and no model requests. It reports 168 policy-budget trajectories, not an empirical sample size of 168 independent histories. All twelve templates improve at least one saved score after correction, but the rescore-only procedure leaves all current states unrecovered. Fresh development executions also expose endpoint non-equivalence: twelve successful candidate invocations in each unrestricted selection arm yield only four initial-input successes. The fixture's memorizing candidate explains that constructed generalization failure.

At budget eight, neutral joint and selective joint both have four initial successes and four later-input successes out of twelve. Without lesson suspension the corresponding selection procedures have four initial successes and two later-input successes, giving a conditional maintenance-failure value of 2/4. Procedures with no initial successes have null conditional maintenance failure. These results do not demonstrate a general advantage of lineage-first repair.

sections.heading: A strong neutral baseline limits the policy claim
paragraphs: The terminal-count tie does not justify declaring all procedures equivalent: realized cost and collateral capability remain outcomes. Table 3 shows the joint procedures. Under cap five, neutral joint has the same four initial and four later-input successes, spends three rather than five authored units on average, and preserves the unaffected task in all twelve histories rather than four. Under cap eight, terminal counts and collateral loss tie, with lower authored spending for selective joint. This reversal is why we do not claim general lineage-first superiority.

The selected procedure follows an authored hint. In the six aligned-hint histories its later-input success is 4/6 versus 2/6 for neutral joint; in the six misleading-hint histories it is 0/6 versus 2/6. Aggregate equality is partly a consequence of the deliberately balanced construction. The same-artifact lesson fork provides a narrower mechanism contrast: two of twelve retain/suspend pairs improve on the later input and ten do not. The programmed lesson rule explains this result; it is not a discovered causal property of real model memory.

sections.heading: Fresh state audits reveal two directions of sampling error
paragraphs: The successful follow-up reconstructs all 168 trajectories and makes 292 fresh state subprocess calls, producing 876 panel outputs with no failed calls. Every comparable same-state output agrees with the prior observation. The earlier coarse protocol made 840 checkpoint audit calls on these trajectories; its additional 24 fixed-artifact memory-audit calls are excluded from that schedule comparison. The 292 count exploits deterministic within-trajectory state identity, so it is not a universal audit-cost advantage for stochastic agents. Observed subprocess duration sums to approximately 57.30 seconds in this execution, without a controlled latency comparison.

Sixteen trajectories have positive initial-area discrepancies, each exactly 0.2; the other 152 have zero difference. All positive cases are budget-five procedures with successful integration at cost four. Per procedure, four of twelve templates change from coarse initial mean zero to committed-state mean 1/15. At budget eight the corresponding initial mean remains 1/6 because integration is grid-aligned. Each positive initial discrepancy attains its trajectory's geometry bound. Terminal success counts remain exactly those of v11.

Later-input utility exposes a separate timing issue. At budget five, joint repair can suspend a harmful lesson only at the cap five. That increases the final later-input success count from two to four without adding positive-duration utility after that last treatment. The committed-state later-input mean is consequently 1/30 for both single-selection and joint procedures at that budget. At budget eight, joint repair's later-input area changes from 1/8 under coarse observation to 7/48 under the full commit path, because lesson suspension occurs at five between the coarse points four and six.

Unaffected-task utility has negative discrepancies in 32 trajectories and zero in 136. For example, at budget five the selective-joint mean drops from coarse unaffected utility 1 to committed-state utility 13/15, while neutral joint remains at 1. Under known complete commit times they therefore identify the same exact areas as the all-observed view. This does not vindicate a left-held coarse interpolation or identify missing commit times. It shows why omission must be defined globally: treating a state as unknown in one path while revealing its identical deterministic outcome elsewhere would manufacture uncertainty.

sections.heading: utility-blind ordering on complete known paths
paragraphs: For a fixed budget and neutral-minus-selective contrast, each complete state has a signed occupation coefficient c_s. Under the same binary audit-only information model, an unrevealed state contributes interval width |c_s|. Revealing one state eliminates exactly that term and discloses all three fixed-panel utilities. Therefore selecting the q largest absolute coefficients minimizes remaining width among all q-state audit sets. The result concerns width, not expected predictive value or a learned audit policy.

The proof is a finite exchange argument. If a selected state has smaller absolute coefficient than an unselected state, swapping them cannot increase the removed width. Repeating such exchanges gives decreasing absolute coefficient order. Ties use ascending SHA-256. Zero coefficients are queried last. At q equal to the number of nonzero coefficients the direct contrast is exact, even when separately identified policy areas still require more states.

We compare three utility-blind schedules: target_abs_coefficient, separately for each budget; cross_budget_l1_coefficient, which sorts by the sum of absolute coefficients over budgets five and eight; and state_hash. A fixed complete-state audit reveals initial, later and unaffected panel values together at one quote unit. Because coefficients depend on path occupation and policy weights rather than the panel score, no panel utility is needed to form an order.

The global cross-budget score is a sharing compromise, not a guarantee of optimality for each individual budget. Audit outputs are reused by complete state identity under a deterministic worker and fixed panel inputs. We do not charge three queries for three panel values, and do not count a state occurring in many of the 168 paths as many distinct new audits. Query quote units are an explicit synthetic cost model; no actual worker or audit execution is made in this replay.

Input bytes, plan and exact code are frozen in a new directory before the query sequence is analyzed. We reuse all 168 earlier complete paths from 12 authored histories and nine unique states. The coefficients include equal weights over all twelve templates and preserve every path. Six target contracts comprise two budgets times three panels, and each schedule is evaluated at all ten prefixes q=0 through9. The resulting 180 rows are dependent audit diagnostics, not 180 policy trials.

sections.heading: Width optimality does not imply minimum sign-certificate cost
paragraphs: We exhaust every q-state subset for both target budgets and verify the greedy prefix width against its exact minimum in twenty cardinality checks. All 180 replay intervals contain the complete-data contrast and shrink monotonically as audits are revealed. A second implementation reconstructs occupation coefficients from the raw paths and checks every bound against 18,414 compatible binary completions. These are alternative computations on the same authored data, not independent scientific replication.

Target coefficient order identifies the exact contrast after five state queries at budget five and four at budget eight. Hash order requires seven and eight respectively. The cross-budget shared order needs five and six. The latter's extra budget-eight queries expose a real multi-target allocation tension: one order serving two contrasts can be less efficient for one target than its individually optimal order. These are exact quote counts in the fixed known-path model; they do not measure physical or model-inference savings.

A stopping rule may inspect revealed bounds and stop when the lower endpoint is strictly positive, the upper endpoint strictly negative, or the interval is a point. It cannot inspect unrevealed utilities. The initial and later true contrasts are zero, so all schedules must reach a point to certify that exact tie. The unaffected panel has positive truth; target coefficient order certifies strict neutral advantage at q=4 for budget five and q=3 for budget eight. Hash order takes q=5 and q=7, and the cross-budget order q=4 for both.

Exhaustive hindsight subset search needs only three audits to certify positive unaffected contrast at either budget. Thus the budget-five width-optimal schedule takes one extra query relative to the outcome-informed optimum. This does not contradict width optimality: sign certification depends on the revealed values and the direction of coefficients, while width depends only on coefficient magnitudes. Retrospective minima cannot be reported as a utility-blind scheduler's realized cost.

The observed true contrast remains the original authored-fixture outcome. No neutral policy receives a new success credit because the audit schedule is efficient. Likewise a narrower interval does not improve the underlying recovery worker. This continuation changes which already saved state audits need to be read to support a statement, not what policy did to the current implementation or lesson memory.

Hash and cross-budget orders are controls. All costs are distinct-state query quotes from cached audit replay; no new audits, unknown-future-path trial or latency measurements.

sections.heading: Information available before a query is the decisive boundary
paragraphs: The word prospective must be scoped carefully. The order is fixed before disclosing the state utilities in this replay, but the complete trajectories and commit times already exist and their earlier outcomes have been exposed to the researchers. The schedule is implementable for a post-run auditing task with fixed known paths. It is not presently a scheduler that chooses audits while recovery is still making unknown future commits.

For an online recovery auditor, a new state changes the future occupation coefficients, and its duration is unknown until the next commit or terminal budget. An order computed from complete future paths would leak information unavailable at that decision time. A faithful online extension would need a predictable allocation rule based on current logs, an explicit update of coefficient uncertainty and a stopping definition valid under changing path geometry. That extension was not implemented or claimed here.

All direct-bound guarantees also require complete commit logs, complete state identity, deterministic fixed-input utilities and no hidden mutation between logged states. Hash equality alone does not prove semantic equivalence or determinism. If hidden commits or stochastic audit drift are possible, the v14 failure counterexamples remain active and a narrow shared-state interval can be invalid. A scheduler must not conceal a failed identification assumption by continuing to report precise bounds.

A genuine resource evaluation should log model/worker invocations, elapsed time, cache lookups and failed queries in addition to unique-state quote units, and preserve natural histories with evaluator corrections rather than constructing only known arithmetic defects. Those records remain absent. The next admissible step is a fully instrumented natural-history run with complete current-state audits and a known-path audit order fixed before audit outcomes are revealed; long-term recurrence and online scheduling require additional independent designs.

sections.heading: auditing without future commits
paragraphs: A deployable audit decision cannot depend on a commit that has not arrived. V15's known-path coefficient order remains a valid offline comparison, but it cannot be used unchanged when the final occupation coefficients are unknown. V16 therefore executes three explicitly causal decision rules through a prefix-only interface, while retaining the earlier signed-state target and every authored-template denominator. The change concerns audit information allocation; it does not create another recovery worker or new failure histories.

For each recovery horizon B in {5,8}, the evaluator reveals all commits through integer checkpoint t, then permits at most one distinct-state quote. The total quote cap is q in {1,2,3,4}. A quote returns the three cached fixed-panel utilities for one observed complete state. The recovery stream is fixed and does not wait for the audit. One quote per checkpoint is a stipulated opportunity constraint, not measured asynchronous latency; these extra audit quote units are not subtracted from the original recovery cost horizon. Identical arrivals, opportunities and caps apply to every competing rule.

The policy sees only timestamps and SHA-256 state identities already visible through t, the completed-prefix signed occupation coefficients, the currently active arm-state frequency difference, and its previously quoted identities. Future commits, terminal coefficients, unrevealed utility values and state program semantics are absent from the decision interface. Utilities enter only the subsequent bound computation after a query has been selected. The evaluator may inspect the saved full trace to score a decision, but that capability is not passed to the policy.

The prefix occupation coefficient d_s(t) averages over all twelve templates in each arm and integrates only completed recovery cost [0,t). Its normalization remains the full fixed horizon B, rather than renormalizing the partial trajectory to one. Thus prefix utility and the remaining future contribution add to the original final contrast. The currently active frequency coefficient a_s(t) describes only the arm difference at t; using it to rank a query does not assert that the state will persist.

The first_seen baseline eagerly queries the earliest arriving unaudited identity, including identities whose present coefficient cancels. The prefix_abs rule queries the largest nonzero |d_s(t)|, while current_disagreement queries the largest nonzero |a_s(t)|; each skips if no eligible identity exists and breaks ties by ascending SHA-256. These simple rules require neither a utility prior nor a learned model. They are predeclared heuristics under changing future weights, rather than optimal adaptive sampling policies.
equations: d_s(t) = (1 / (12 B)) sum_(h=1)^12 integral_0^t (bold(1)[S_(h,N)(z)=s] - bold(1)[S_(h,L)(z)=s]) dif z

sections.heading: Unknown-suffix bounds and an unavoidable sign ambiguity
paragraphs: Even exhaustive audits of already observed states do not reveal an unknown future path. At checkpoint t, we bound each policy's remaining normalized utility contribution between zero and r_t=(B-t)/B. Their difference is therefore in [-r_t,r_t]. Adding this suffix to the shared-state prefix interval gives a valid final-contrast interval without assuming that future states belong to the nine identities eventually present in the saved files. This is an outer bound for the online information model; we claim sharpness only for the terminal fixed-path audit interval when r_t=0.

For a quoted-state set O_t, let K_t be the signed prefix sum over revealed utilities. The lower endpoint adds negative unknown prefix coefficients to K_t and subtracts r_t; the upper endpoint adds positive unknown prefix coefficients and r_t. The same state/input deterministic equivalence assumption enables a quoted value to be reused when that state reappears. Hidden state mutation, incomplete commit logs or changing fixed-panel outputs invalidate this reuse and remain unresolved empirical admission conditions.

An explicit two-world construction illustrates why the future term cannot simply be deleted. Let B=4 and observe checkpoint t=1. Both arms have occupied the same audited utility-1/2 state, and no further commit has yet arrived. In one compatible completion, at cost 2 the neutral arm moves to utility 1 and the selective arm to utility 0; in the other, their future utilities are exchanged. The terminal contrasts are +1/2 and -1/2. Both completions agree with every observation through t=1. The stipulated prefix interval is [-3/4,3/4], containing both outcomes; its width is not claimed to be the tightest interval for a more restricted transition system.

Consequently, no rule using only that common prefix can universally certify the final sign. This is a constructive information limit, not a claim that every online instance is unidentifiable. A restricted future transition graph, minimum dwell times, or a validated stochastic transition model could tighten the suffix. None is silently inferred from the exposed nine-state fixture. The witness is a separate analytic construction and is not counted as two additional empirical histories.
